overview: The two broad kingdoms of human parasites, split by something as basic as being single-celled or not.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Single-celled eukaryotic parasites capable of active movement and, in some cases, intracellular replication within the host.
aspects.valueB: Multicellular worm parasites (flatworms and roundworms) that generally live extracellularly in the host.

aspects.label: Replication in Host
aspects.valueA: Many can multiply within the human host, sometimes leading to overwhelming infection from a small inoculum.
aspects.valueB: Adult worms generally do not multiply in the human host; worm burden depends on repeated exposure.

aspects.label: Diagnostic Approach
aspects.valueA: Microscopic identification of trophozoites/cysts in stool, blood, or tissue; some require special stains.
aspects.valueB: Identification of eggs, larvae, or adult worms in stool, blood, or tissue; egg morphology is often diagnostic.

aspects.label: Classic Examples
aspects.valueB: Ascaris lumbricoides, Taenia species, Schistosoma species.

aspects.label: Association With Eosinophilia
aspects.valueA: Not typically associated with marked eosinophilia.
aspects.valueB: Tissue-invasive helminth infections classically cause marked eosinophilia.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Single-celled, can multiply within the host.
aspects.valueB: Multicellular, generally does not multiply within the host.
